&2010
Metropolia University of Applied Sciences led with a 10 percent share of all theses.
Health, welfare, and sports remained the dominant academic field, capturing one-third of all research.
Engineering and transport fields maintained strong output, representing nearly a quarter of total publications.
Business, administration, and social sciences continued as the third most popular field for students.
Cultural and service sectors remained stable, providing significant contributions to the overall institutional research volume.

&2011
Oulu University of Applied Sciences temporarily surged to the top position in annual thesis output.
Health and welfare fields continued to expand, solidifying their status as the primary focus area.
Engineering sectors remained steady, consistently producing one-quarter of the total annual research volume.
Business and social sciences showed consistent growth in academic interest among university students.
Smaller fields like humanities and education began to see minor shifts in their relative research impact.

&2012
Metropolia University regained its position as the leading institution for thesis production in Finland.
Health and welfare fields maintained dominance, accounting for over 33 percent of all submitted work.
Business and administrative studies grew slightly, closing the gap with the engineering and technology sectors.
Research output across major universities remained concentrated within the top five performing institutions.
Cultural studies experienced a slight decline in relative share as interdisciplinary interests began to evolve.

&2013
Metropolia University continued its dominance, extending its lead over other major Finnish applied science institutions.
Health, welfare, and sports fields maintained their core position, comprising one-third of all academic output.
Business, administration, and law studies saw consistent demand, solidifying their role in the national curriculum.
Engineering and technology output remained stable, continuing to form a significant pillar of university research.
Cultural arts and service sectors held consistent, though smaller, shares of the total research landscape.

&2014
Metropolia University maintained its status as the top producer of theses among all applied institutions.
Health, welfare, and sports fields continued to lead, capturing approximately one-third of total research volume.
Business and administrative sciences reached a new high, reflecting increased focus on social and economic studies.
Engineering and technology sectors showed slight stabilization, remaining a core area for university degree programs.
Natural sciences began to show a modest upward trend in the proportion of completed student theses.

&2015
Metropolia University remained the national leader, holding over 11 percent of all thesis production volume.
Health and social fields accounted for over 34 percent of all research, marking a historical peak.
Engineering sectors maintained a significant presence, though faced growing competition from social and business fields.
Business and administrative studies showed robust growth, continuing to attract a large segment of students.
Research output across the top ten universities remained highly consolidated among a few major institutions.

&2016
Metropolia University continued to lead, with output growing to represent nearly 12 percent of all theses.
Health and welfare fields remained the largest academic category, encompassing over one-third of total production.
Business and administration emerged as the second largest field as classification systems began to modernize.
Engineering and technology sectors experienced a relative decline in total share compared to earlier years.
Information technology started to be tracked more distinctly, signaling its growing importance in academic research.

&2017
Metropolia University expanded its lead, accounting for 12.4 percent of total thesis output nationally.
Health and welfare fields surged to represent 37 percent of all academic work produced this year.
Business and administrative fields maintained a steady 21 percent share of the total research landscape.
Engineering and technology output experienced a slight dip as institutions pivoted toward newer digital specializations.
Information technology and communication studies became more prominent as dedicated fields within the degree programs.

&2018
Metropolia University maintained its position at the top, supported by strong volume in health and technology.
Health and welfare sectors remained dominant, comprising over 36 percent of the national thesis output.
Business and administration continued to command a large share, remaining the second most popular field.
Engineering output showed signs of recovery, with a slight increase in total thesis volume recorded.
Information and communication technology continued to grow as an independent and significant area of research.

&2019
Metropolia University remained the primary academic leader, consistently producing over 3,000 theses annually.
Health and welfare studies continued to dominate, despite a slight decrease in total percentage share.
Business and administration maintained a strong 20 percent share, anchoring the national academic research output.
Engineering remained a primary field, showing resilience despite changing industry and academic focus areas.
Information and communication technology reached a new high, reflecting its expanding role in modern curriculum.

&2020
Metropolia University continued to lead, maintaining an 11 percent share of the total national output.
Health and welfare fields remained central, even as total thesis volumes fluctuated during the year.
Business and administration saw a notable increase, becoming a more prominent focus for university students.
Engineering and technology fields maintained a stable presence within the top three academic categories.
Information and communication technology continued to grow, solidifying its place as a key academic field.

&2021
Metropolia University maintained its top position, with Haaga-Helia growing its share among the leading institutions.
Health and welfare fields saw a significant resurgence, accounting for 35 percent of all thesis work.
Business and administration remained the second most popular research field among Finnish university students.
Engineering and technology continued to provide a stable foundation for the bulk of academic research projects.
Information and communication technology maintained its upward trajectory as a critical area for degree completion.

&2022
Metropolia University remained the leader, though other institutions began to narrow the output gap.
Health and welfare fields continued to represent the largest single category of academic research produced.
Business and administration maintained strong performance, reflecting consistent student interest in economic and social sciences.
Engineering and technology sectors showed steady output, remaining essential to the national thesis production profile.
Information and communication technology continued to hold steady, supported by ongoing digital transformation in education.

&2023
Metropolia University maintained its top position while Laurea University showed significant growth in thesis production.
Health, welfare, and sports sectors continued to dominate, capturing over 35 percent of all research.
Business, administration, and law fields reached a new peak in share, indicating high demand for graduates.
Engineering fields remained core to the academic landscape despite a slight drop in relative total share.
Information and communication technology reached 8 percent, marking its strongest year for thesis output to date.

&2024
Metropolia University reached a new high in total thesis volume, leading the national research landscape.
Health and welfare remained the primary field, growing significantly in absolute numbers of finished theses.
Business and administrative studies continued to climb, capturing nearly 23 percent of all student research.
Engineering output remained robust, contributing significantly to the total volume despite changing educational priorities.
Information and communication technology surged to 8.6 percent, reflecting rapid technological integration into university programs.

&2025
Metropolia University solidified its leadership, accounting for over 3,700 theses within the current academic year.
Health and welfare sectors grew further, continuing their trend as the dominant research field nationally.
Business, administration, and law studies accounted for 23 percent of all research produced this year.
Information and communication technology reached a record 9.4 percent, signaling massive growth in digital expertise.
Engineering remained a vital field, maintaining a large, stable share of total academic thesis output.
